sentences.text: Chubutisaurus possessed a more robust radius bone compared to the dinosaur Venenosaurus.
Gregory S. Paul estimated Chubutisaurus to be 18 meters long and weigh 12 tons in 2010, while Thomas Holtz estimated the length at 23 meters in 2012.
The species name insignis means "remarkable" in Latin.
The name Chubutisaurus combines the province of Chubut where it was found with the Greek word for lizard.
Fossils of Chubutisaurus were first discovered in 1961 by a local farmer named Mr. Martinez near El Escorial village in Chubut Province, Argentina.
Guillermo del Corro scientifically described the remains and named the new species Chubutisaurus insignis in 1975.
The holotype specimen of Chubutisaurus consists of a single incomplete and disarticulated individual found across multiple expeditions.
Fossils from the 1991 and 2007 expeditions were cataloged at the Museo Paleontológico 'Egidio Feruglio', meaning the holotype is now split among three institutions.
Chubutisaurus was a somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) period found in the Cerro Barcino Formation of Argentina.
Chubutisaurus was initially placed in the Brachiosauridae but is now considered a primitive titanosaur related to Late Cretaceous dinosaurs.
Chubutisaurus is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
While initially dated to 112-93 million years ago, later dating places Chubutisaurus solely in the Late Cretaceous.

In 1993, paleontologist Leonardo Salgado redescribed Chubutisaurus and reinterpreted it as an indeterminate sauropod. In 2011, Jose Carballido and colleagues described new fossils in detail and concluded they belonged to the same holotype individual. The Paleobi Database lists the time range of Chubutisaurus as Aptian to Albian (119.57 to 110.1 million years ago), which contradicts other sources placing it in the Late Cretaceous.
